master.initial:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Create the corrected master ship illustration for a modular 3D modeling kit. Image 1 is the edit target: preserve its attractive warm textured timber, stylized chunky carved shapes, iron hardware, cream cloth, gray studio backdrop and elevated three-quarter composition, bow at RIGHT, stern at LEFT. Keep a coherent recognizably same pirate ship, not an unrelated redesign. Produce one entire assembled full-color ship with generous margin around everything.

Correct its nautical construction:
1. All working sails are ordinary aged IVORY CANVAS with stitched panels and restrained patches; absolutely NO skull, flag graphic or emblem printed on any sail. Put ONE small separate black Jolly Roger flag at the aft mainmast head, clearly a flag attached by its hoist, not part of a working sail. Remove giant red streamers.
2. A coherent simplified two-masted brig rig: FOREMAST toward the bow/right is shorter; MAINMAST aft/left is taller. Mainmast stands on the main deck just forward of the raised quarterdeck, NOT on the cabin roof. Each mast carries a large lower square sail and a smaller square topsail on transverse yards with a plausible mast-top platform at the lower mast/topmast junction, supported by cross-trees. No barrel baskets balanced on bare mast tips. Plain triangular jib on the stay to the bowsprit. An ivory gaff spanker aft of the mainmast has its boom above crew head height and does not intersect the steering area. Keep rigging simple enough to read, but shrouds, deadeyes, stays and sheets attach to real supports; no floating lines or ladders that end midair.
3. Remove every lantern standing on the quarterdeck railing or beside the helm. One modest enclosed lantern hung OUTSIDE on a stern-facing transom bracket, entirely aft of the wheel, clear of walking areas.
4. Helm aligned fore-aft on the quarterdeck with clear standing room and a small compass binnacle; rudder hinges on sternpost below, not a detached blade. Stern gallery integrates into the hull with curved lower body and modest windows; no tower or cottage roof. One enclosed cabin level above main deck, supported quarterdeck floor as its roof, stairs connect the two walkable floors.
5. Use four evenly spaced gun ports on the visible straight middle broadside; iron cannon muzzles emerge from genuine openings with hinged port lids. No iron strap crossing a gunport; shroud chainplates fall between ports. Keep working deck paths clear. Anchor hangs from a proper forward cathead outside the hull, cable leads through a hawse opening to the capstan. No anchor draped across a gun muzzle.
6. Timber plank seams and wooden wales define the hull construction; dark metal hardware is localized to brackets, bolts and fittings, NOT a cage of huge metal hoops encircling the ship. Bow closed and symmetric, rounded stern, full curved hull and keel visible. Reusable straight midship rail bays and repeated gun bays are visibly consistent, with dedicated curved end pieces.

The illustration is a finished textured modeling concept in the same stylized toon game style: broad painted light/shadow planes, clear planks with sparse grain, warm oak/chestnut timber, matte dark iron, restrained brass, tan rope. Full ship on neutral pale warm-gray background. No sea or land, no people, no exploded kit, no text, no dimensions. Favor logical readable attachments over ornament. Do not crop mastheads, keel, stern, or bowsprit.
The side cannon ports serve a continuous enclosed lower gun deck, with its floor and a companionway down from the main deck. They must not open into a solid hull or through the bilge. Readable deck hierarchy: lower gun deck, open main deck above it, small stern cabin and quarterdeck only aft.

The short extra vertical post currently rising beside the helm underneath the leftmost angled gaff is incorrect here: remove that extra mast. The leftmost fore-and-aft spanker sail must attach directly to the AFT MAINMAST (the tall mast with the pirate flag), with its luff vertical along the aft side of that mast. hull.initial:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production art reference for separately modeling and texturing modular parts of the SAME corrected pirate ship shown in reference image 1. Faithfully reuse that ship's warm oak/chestnut plank palette, broad painted grain, dark seams, faceted bevels, restrained iron brackets and square fasteners. Finished colored toon game asset illustrations, not gray primitives, not photorealism. Neutral pale-gray background, clean generous gutters, each part isolated and fully visible without touching its neighbors. Consistent elevated three-quarter camera and light direction; opaque interior surfaces and clean construction cut ends readable. Short exact part IDs and names under objects in a simple dark sans-serif font. No invented decorative parts. This is a modeling reference sheet, not a dense infographic. Give the art most of the space. Do not show a new ship design. All repeatable profiles in this sheet must match each other. No decorative texture on mating faces, no hardware protruding across a join. Maximal useful resolution, crisp detail, landscape canvas.
SHEET TITLE: "01 — HULL MODULES".
Reference image 2 supplies the structural separation only: match those bow, centre and stern shell families; texture them with the wood of image 1. Arrange a readable 3-column by 4-row matrix. Columns BOW / CENTRE / STERN. Every module is a hollow shell, not a solid block. Show mating edges clearly. Floor/deck panels and cannon barrels are omitted.

Row 1:
"H01 LOWER BOW" — closed symmetric pointed prow with curved bilge bottom, open broad aft join, no walls across the join.
"H02 LOWER CENTRE" — short repeated U-shaped bilge segment with open fore and aft joins.
"H03 LOWER STERN" — curved rounded closed exterior stern with bilge bottom; broad fore join open.
Row 2:
"H04 MIDDLE BOW" — same pointed outline above H01, constant-height side walls, no floor, open aft join.
"H05 GUN BAY" — TWO opposite matching wall panels, one real rectangular gun opening per side, no floor or connecting end wall. Frame around opening, no cannon, no hatch lid filling the hole.
"H06 MIDDLE STERN" — constant-height curved stern wall, no floor, no roof, no raised feature or cabin, open fore join.
Row 3:
"H08 TOP BOW" — shallow low shaped bow bulwark, no tall posts.
"H09 TOP CENTRE" — pair of shallow straight low bulwark panels.
"H10 TOP STERN" — shallow curved low stern bulwark matching H06, no cabin or raised portions.
Row 4:
"H07 SOLID BAY" — pair of solid wall panels with same profile as H05 but no openings.
"H11 GUNPORT LID" — separate rectangular hinged plank lid shown open and detached from any wall.
"H12 WOODEN WALE" — repeatable broad timber hull reinforcing strip with clearly straight butt ends, wood rather than a giant iron hoop.

Do not bake floors or railings into shell modules. All middle walls same vertical height; top walls same low height; matching outline per longitudinal column. The lower bow and stern need end closures only on the exterior end, NEVER a bulkhead across the midship join. Use three-quarter orientations that let us see the empty interior and join, not only exterior facades. The middle stern must look like a plain curved wall, with nothing sticking up. A small footer reads "Shared joins • Separate floors • Repeat centre bays".
hull.revision:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Revise the supplied HULL MODULES sheet only in these targeted ways, preserving the 12 cells, all labels, neutral background, wood/iron material style and all correct centre/ stern panels.

CRITICAL: Completely redraw the three BOW cells H01, H04 and H08 from a perfectly centered slightly elevated FRONT/BOW VIEW, symmetric about their vertical centerline, just like the bow silhouettes in reference image 2. Each is a SINGLE clean V-shaped pair of port/starboard shell walls meeting seamlessly at one central closed pointed prow. The two open-ended wall arms extend equally backwards left and right; there is absolutely NO third wall across the aft join, NO interior transverse bulkhead, NO overlapping doubled prow, NO extra short wall sticking toward the viewer. Empty interior/background visible behind the V. H01 adds only the curved bilge bottom below those matching side walls, with open upper interior; H04 is a CONSTANT HEIGHT V-shaped band of walls with no floor/bottom; H08 is a LOW V-shaped bulwark strip, no floor. Keep the bow symmetric, pointed, and closed ONLY at its central prow tip. Use the same outline for all three rows.

H06 MIDDLE STERN must be a simple CONSTANT HEIGHT curved U/C-shaped wall band with parallel top and bottom boundaries, NO bilge rounding below it, NO floor, no raised aft portion. H03 alone has the rounded bilge bottom. Matching open fore cut of H03/H06/H10.

All other content unchanged. If a bow drawn from three-quarter view would be ambiguous, use the symmetric centered bow-on view, not perspective trickery. These are visual modeling references, not dimensionally certified meshes.

SHEET TITLE: "02 — DECKS & RAILINGS".
Image 2 is the EXACT footprint reference for bow, centre and stern floors. No flooring asset may have a railing, raised wall, curb or decorative post attached. Show 12 labeled cells arranged 4 columns x 3 rows:

"D01 BOW DECK" — flat thin planked slab, symmetric tapered pointed bow footprint from image 2; broad straight aft edge. Nothing sticking up.
"D02 CENTRE DECK" — flat rectangular planked slab, full interior beam wide and one short repeating bay long; clean matching butt edges. No posts.
"D03 STERN DECK" — flat shallow half-ellipse slab, straight forward join and rounded aft perimeter, matching image 2. No posts.
"D04 MAST OPENING" — same rectangular slab as D02 but a real centered circular mast aperture, show empty hole, collar detached above it. No mast.
"D05 HATCH OPENING" — same slab with a clean rectangular OPEN hole, coaming shown separately beside it, no grate blocking the hole.
"D06 STAIR OPENING PAIR" — two consecutive floor segments together with a long rectangular opening crossing their shared join, a dashed seam visible; no stairs built into floor.
"D07 BEAM & KNEES" — isolated underside cross-deck timber beam with separate L-shaped curved support knees; no posts.
"R01 STRAIGHT INFILL" — low straight rail infill bay: horizontal top/bottom timber with matching turned balusters. NO full-height terminal posts attached; butt ends meet R02. No floor.
"R02 SHARED POST" — one separate sturdy square corner/terminal post with sockets for R01, used once at each join, same wood/iron style.
"R03 BOW RAIL PAIR" — mirrored left/right curved-tapered low rail infills, made for matching bow edges, no floor or terminal posts.
"R04 STERN RAIL" — curved low rail infill matching shallow rounded stern edge, no floor or terminal posts.
"R05 STAIR RAIL" — one sloping rail infill matched to a staircase incline, separate from stairs and terminal posts.

Deck plank grain runs fore-aft and plank widths are consistent across every D tile. Deck edges are plain butt joints, floor slabs remain thin and flat, projected geometry follows the source floor shapes. Railing infills use the SAME low baluster spacing and height as ship image 1; avoid random fence designs. Add small footer: "Floors separate • One post per join • Shaped end pieces".

SHEET TITLE: "03 — CABIN & QUARTERDECK".
Eight large cells, four columns by two rows. First cell is an assembled example of the aft cabin only, other seven show isolated removable parts. Reuse precisely the ship reference's arched blue-glass windows, warm planking, restrained dark iron, broad trim and chunky bevels. Cabin is ONE supported level, with its roof acting as the walkable raised quarterdeck, not a house roof. No wheels, lanterns or sails baked into structure.

Cell 1 "ASSEMBLED CABIN" — same compact aft cabin from ship reference with front access door, side windows, curved aft exterior, walkable flat roof/quarterdeck and its separate stairs. Small demonstration without full hull or mast.
"C01 DOOR WALL" — flat bulkhead panel with real framed doorway; door leaf shown separately next to it.
"C02 WINDOW WALL" — repeatable flat wall bay with one arched framed glazed window, thick matching top/bottom trim and clean side joins.
"C03 AFT CORNER PAIR" — left/right matched curved transition wall panels connecting the straight side walls to the aft transom; no roof and no floor.
"C04 TRANSOM WALL" — a curved stern-facing wall with three arched windows, same height and trim course as C02/C03; top flat for roof attachment; no railing baked in.
"C05 QUARTERDECK PANELS" — two or three thin flat roof/deck panels laid apart by narrow gaps, together matching cabin footprint with curved stern end and straight front; show matching beam support underneath one, no roof tiles, railings or posts.
"C06 QUARTERDECK STAIRS" — one separately modeled wooden stair flight on two stringers, freestanding without walls, opens onto a clear landing; handrails are separate assets from R05. No solid heavy cube under steps.
"C07 GALLERY BRACKETS" — pair of short sturdy carved timber support knees with local iron bolts, for small stern gallery/quarterdeck projection; no whole building.

Show matching wall thickness, panel height, continuous plank/trim courses and clean butt joints throughout. Nothing floats in the assembled example; quarterdeck supported by cabin walls and beams, stairs reach its top surface and do not end against a railing. Footer: "One cabin level • Roof is quarterdeck • Separate walls, floor and stairs".

SHEET TITLE: "04 — MASTS, SAILS & RIGGING".
Create 16 generously separated cells in a four-by-four layout, high-resolution. These parts all belong to the same two-masted vessel shown in the reference. All working sails are plain aged IVORY cloth, seams and restrained repair patches, no printed emblems. The only skull graphic belongs on a SEPARATE small black flag.

Row 1:
"M01 FOREMAST" — shorter tapered lower mast shaft, heel and masthead join visible, no sail or crow's nest baked in.
"M02 MAINMAST" — taller matching lower shaft, same construction, mainmast belongs aft. No sail or top platform baked in.
"M03 TOPMAST" — smaller tapered upper mast segment with clearly shaped joining heel and cap fitting shown separately.
"M04 MAST TOP" — shallow open wooden top platform with central mast aperture, supported by trestletrees and cross-trees below; no deep basket and no mast shaft.
Row 2:
"M05 LOWER YARD" — broad tapered transverse wooden spar with center sling band and end attachment eyes.
"M06 TOPSAIL YARD" — shorter matching transverse spar.
"M07 BOWSPRIT" — thick tapered forward spar with heel socket, iron bands only where structurally needed.
"M08 GAFF & BOOM (OPTIONAL)" — detached matching upper gaff with curved jaws and lower boom with gooseneck; no extra standing mast.
Row 3:
"S01 LOWER SQUARE SAIL" — isolated ivory course cloth, shaped broad trapezoid, boltrope hem and corner eyes, no spar or mast attached.
"S02 TOPSAIL" — smaller trapezoidal ivory square topsail with reinforced corners, no spar.
"S03 JIB" — isolated triangular ivory sail with three reinforced corner attachment points and boltrope.
"S04 SPANKER (OPTIONAL)" — isolated fore-and-aft trapezoidal ivory gaff sail with vertical luff and corner eyes, no mast or spars.
Row 4:
"S05 PIRATE FLAG" — small standalone black rectangular flag with ivory skull and crossbones, separate edge hoist loops. Clearly a flag, not a working sail.
"G01 SHROUDS & RATLINES" — tapered panel of several taut ropes with horizontal rope rungs and deadeyes below, not a wooden ladder.
"G02 STAYS & SHEETS" — isolated restrained selection of taut rope runs with endpoint eyes and one coil; depict ropes as separate adaptable curves, not a rigid net or floating crossed mess.
"G03 BLOCKS & DEADEYES" — three well-spaced component examples: single-sheave wooden pulley block, double block, round three-hole deadeye with lanyard; clear pass-through holes.

Match the finished ship's proportion language and materials, functional visible attachment features, no architectural walls or floors. A small footer states "Cloth separate from spars • Rigging adapts to hull length • Optional aft sail". The optional gaff/spanker combination attaches directly to the aft mainmast, not a third mast.
rig.revision:

SHEET TITLE: "05 — WORKING FITTINGS".
Ten component cards arranged across the top in two rows of five, plus two larger functional assembly insets below. All fittings belong to the corrected ship in image 1. Show complete usable attachment hardware, not floating disconnected decorations.

Cards:
"F01 CANNON BARREL" — short matte dark iron naval barrel with round muzzle bore and two transverse trunnions, isolated.
"F02 GUN CARRIAGE" — low sturdy wooden four-truck naval carriage, iron straps, trunnion bearing recesses, elevating wedge and breeching rope eyes, no barrel attached.
"F03 HELM" — wooden spoke wheel, axle drum and substantial paired timber supports, wheel and pedestal clearly separate objects.
"F04 BINNACLE" — compact nautical compass cabinet with visible compass bowl under glazed brass cover, placed ahead of helm in use, not an oversized lamp.
"F05 CAPSTAN" — vertical wooden rope-handling drum with removable horizontal capstan bars, dark iron hardware, base bearing.
"F06 RUDDER" — timber blade with straight upper rudder stock and visible alternating pintle/gudgeon hinge fittings; no wheel attached.
"F07 ANCHOR SET" — iron stocked anchor, separate stout wooden cathead with a pulley and lifting tackle, heavy tan anchor cable; all three pieces readable with air gaps.
"F08 STERN LANTERN" — one small enclosed metal/glass lantern and separate outboard-facing bracket that bolts to the exterior transom, not a railing-top pedestal.
"F09 HATCH SET" — removable wooden grating alongside a separate raised timber coaming; coaming interior open.
"F10 BELAYING FITTINGS" — three small examples side by side: timber belaying-pin rack, a cleat, a paired wooden bollard/bitts. Do not merge them.

Bottom inset 1 "GUN BAY ASSEMBLY" — short cutaway of one wood gunport with lifted separate lid, cannon seated by its trunnions in F02 carriage on a real lower gun-deck floor, clear interior space behind the gun for recoil and working. No cannon through a solid plank; no rope or iron band crosses the muzzle.
Bottom inset 2 "STERN STEERING" — small diagram-like textured cutaway at the stern, wheel on clear aft deck, a rope/steering linkage routed below deck to a tiller on the rudder stock, rudder hinged to sternpost, exterior stern lantern mounted outside and away from wheel. No front-facing outline of objects, no full new ship.

Use same established timber palette, iron and brass balance and proportions throughout. Header and IDs only, no long paragraphs. Footer: "Moving parts separate • Clear working space • Supported attachments".

hull_sheet_replacement.method: No image generation. tools/render_textured.py renders textured/meshes/*.glb (canonical geometry plus UVs) with one camera and one scale.
hull_sheet_replacement.why: The painted sheet contradicted the contract: H02 drawn with a rocker and a wall across its join, H03 as a canoe, H10 with a raised end. Contract: H02 is a straight U-section, closed bilge below, both longitudinal ends open; H09 two straight parallel low walls; H10 a constant-height rounded aft closure open toward the centre.
hull_sheet_replacement.albedo: Procedural and seeded (tools/texture_kit.py, recipe in textured/texture-recipe.json); flat colour, no baked light.
